formulas.ascii: Label phase, after the cost search: on every tight edge u->v (f32 equality costs[u] + w == costs[v], no tolerance, zero-weight edges included) labels[v] = min(labels[v], labels[u]) with an atomic minimum, seeded at the facility nodes. The fixpoint is the smallest facility row among all facilities that reach v at its minimum cost, independent of thread order. Unreached nodes keep NONE (0xffffffff).

symbols.label: label of the edge source u

formulas.ascii: hopDistances[v] = cost[v] <= limit ? uint(cost[v]) : NONE, where cost is the unit-weight search cost, limit = min(hops, maximumHops) and NONE = 0xffffffff. NaN and +Infinity costs compare false and stay outside the ego network.

Per edge sample at fraction t along u->v and per pixel within the buffer radius: cost = abs(sourceCost + t*weight + walk*pixelDistance); each pixel keeps the minimum cost over all samples (min mode; atomic minimum on order-preserving f32 bits, so the result does not depend on thread order). Samples are linear along straight segments between node positions, so this is a sampled raster, not an exact polygonal travel-time boundary; pixels no sample reaches stay unreached.

band = first k with time < bandBreaks[k], else 0xffffffff (no band). Upper bounds are strict; unreached, unsnapped or non-finite demand times (>= 3.0e38) get no band. time = min(cost[source] + sourceCost, cost[target] + targetCost) on the snapped edge, from the demand-time kernel.

For each point p the scan visits every edge row e in ascending order and keeps the edge with the smallest point-to-segment distance d(p,e): bestEdge = e when bestEdge is NONE or d < bestDistance (strict, so ties go to the smallest edge row; NaN never wins). Distances are in the spatial context length unit (meters for a great-circle longitude/latitude context); with a maximum snap distance, edges beyond it are skipped and an unsnapped point gets NONE.

Exponential-decay variant, opportunity-rows orientation: for every column node j the kernel sums rows i in ascending order and adds weight[i] * exp(-beta * cost[i,j]) for finite costs 0 <= cost <= threshold and finite weights (unreached +Infinity entries and non-finite weights are skipped; the sum is deterministic, no float atomics, and weights are not normalised). The cumulative variant omits the decay and the power variant uses max(cost, minimumCost)^-beta; they are alternative branches of the same kernel.

normalized = highest > lowest ? (raw - lowest) / (highest - lowest) : 0, in f32. lowest and highest are the two words of the extent reduction (minimum, maximum of the raw column over all nodes); a column with a single value (no range) normalizes to 0 for every node. The raw degree is the outgoing CSR row length from the degree algorithm.

closeness = totalCost > 0 ? (reachedPartial[0] - 1) / totalCost : 0, per pivot. Outward closeness: totalCost is the f32 sum of the search costs of every node the pivot reaches (infinite costs are skipped), added by a fixed 256-lane tree reduction so the value does not depend on thread order. reachedPartial[0] counts the reached nodes including the pivot itself. The Wasserman-Faust factor (r - 1) / (N - 1) is not applied; the unit is 1 / cost (1 / second on travel-time weights).

localHistogram[getBin(outValue)] += 1 (atomic) for every live node, where outValue is its live out-degree and getBin(d) = min(floor(d / binWidth), BIN_COUNT - 1) for the linear rule (the last bin saturates; log2 binning uses bin 0 for d = 0, else min(1 + floor(log2 d), BIN_COUNT - 1)). Each workgroup then adds its non-empty bins to the summary words, so integer addition makes the histogram independent of thread order. The in-degree and total-degree histograms use the same rule.

For every enabled range, live = live && value >= parameters[base] && value < parameters[base + 1]: half-open, so the maximum itself is excluded, and a NaN value never passes. A disabled range (parameters[base + 2] == 0) is skipped. The mask starts at 1 (or at the caller mask), so the result is the AND of all ranges; an edge slot is finally kept only when both of its endpoints are live, and dropIsolated also removes nodes left without a live slot. Integer and comparison arithmetic only, so the result is exact.

getBin(position, start, end) = (position - start) * RESOLUTION / (end - start) with u32 division (floor). A live slot u -> v adds 1 (atomically) to cell getBin(order[u]) * RESOLUTION + getBin(order[v]): rows are source positions, columns are target positions, and slots whose positions fall outside the window [start, end) are dropped. Counts are exact integers, so the matrix does not depend on thread order; with fewer bins than nodes, each bin covers several consecutive matrix positions.

lineWeights[arc e -> f] = baseCost >= 0 ? baseCost + max(turnCost, 0) : -1, where baseCost = weights[f] is the cost of the NEXT edge f (not of the entering edge e) and turnCost = getTurnCost(e, f) = angleCost * |angle| plus the left or right extra beyond straightAngle; a turn with |angle| >= uTurnAngle pays uTurnCost instead, and a negative uTurnCost bans it (no arc is emitted). Banned pairs are removed too, so every emitted arc has turnCost >= 0. The angle is between the great-circle arrival bearing of e and the departure bearing of f at the turn node, positive to the left. Arcs of one edge are listed in ascending next-edge order.

Table admission, after the cutoff search of one source row: isIncluded = isFiniteBits(cost) && cost >= 0, where cost is the f32 reachability fixpoint searched with the cost limit. Unreached nodes are +Infinity and are not stored; the source itself is stored at cost 0. Included targets are packed in ascending node order by an inclusive scan, so slot order is fixed; entries past the capacity are dropped and reported by the overflow status. This is the admission rule, not a second shortest-path formula.

Exponential decay, the branch chosen by the decay parameter: weights = exp(-beta * cost) for every finite matrix cost with 0 <= cost <= costLimit; other entries (unreached +Infinity, negative, beyond the limit) are not stored. Slots follow ascending neighbor order within each row. The 'none' branch stores 1, 'power' stores max(cost, minimumCost)^-beta and 'gaussian' stores the truncated, rescaled (exp(-0.5 (c/L)^2) - exp(-0.5)) / (1 - exp(-0.5)); they are alternative branches of the same kernel.

K(d_k) = 2 * cumulative * networkLength / (count * count) for count >= 2 snapped events, else 0. cumulative is the number of unordered event pairs whose network distance is strictly below the band threshold d_k = maximumDistance * k / (bandCount - 1) (a prefix sum of the per-band pair histogram); networkLength is the length of every road counted once. The denominator is count squared (the spaghetti GlobalAutoK normalisation), not count * (count - 1). With zero simulations only the observed row exists.

rowWeights[row] = fixed_tree_sum(sortedContributions[begin:end]): one workgroup per stored origin-destination pair sums the pair's contributions (the weights of its records, in source row order, 0 for rejected or non-finite weights) with a strided partial sum and a fixed binary tree, so the float sum is bitwise reproducible. It is a sum of the weights (trips), not a mean and not the record count; flowCounts counts the records of the pair separately.

symbols.label: record weights of the pair, sorted

formulas.tex: \term{costs}{c_v}\leftarrow\min(\term{costs}{c_v},\operatorname{f32}(\term{source}{c_u}+\term{weight}{w_{uv}})),\quad v<\term{count}{N},\ w_{uv}\ge0,\ c_u+w_{uv}\le L;\qquad c_v^*=\min_s(c_s^0+d(s,v))\le L
formulas.ascii: Atomic minimum of non-negative f32 cost bits: c[v] <- min(c[v], f32(c[u] + w[u,v])). Negative/NaN weights are impassable; out-of-range neighbors and non-finite candidates are ignored. With cutoff L, candidates above L stay unreached (+Infinity); without a cutoff L = +Infinity. At convergence c[v] = min_s(c0[s] + d(s,v)), restricted to <= L, with path sums evaluated in f32. Chaotic: a visit may read costs improved earlier in the same round; rounds are not synchronous Bellman-Ford sweeps.
For finite cost <= the last ascending threshold, band = count(threshold < cost); otherwise NONE (0xffffffff). Band 0 includes the first threshold; band i is (threshold[i-1], threshold[i]].
